conventions.convention: The one-dimensional mesh is uniform with N≥1, h=1/N, ε>0 and b≠0. V_h has zero endpoint values; nonzero prescribed endpoints belong to S_h(g_0,g_1).
Pe=|b|h/(2ε) and τ=h/(2|b|)(coth(Pe)−1/Pe). Second derivatives in the residual are cellwise classical derivatives; the smooth consistency extension retains −εw″.
The multidimensional branch has d≥2, matching shape-regular affine simplices, zero data on the entire boundary, b∈C1, c∈C, and c−div(b)/2≥ω>0.
δ_K=θ min{h_K²/ε,h_K/||b||∞,K,ω/||c||∞,K²}, with zero coefficient denominators interpreted as +∞ and 0<θ≤1/4.
The mixed signs are −(p,div v)+(q,div u), PSPG tests the momentum residual against ∇q, and grad-div has nonnegative coefficient γ.

The PSPG coercivity theorem requires strictly positive cell parameters, connected cell adjacency, zero velocity boundary values and continuous mean-zero pressure. Pressure control is only in the mesh-dependent gradient stabilization norm.

VMS is finite-dimensional real block algebra: A_ff is invertible, and T replaces its inverse in both the Schur operator and the Schur load. The defect theorem additionally requires the approximate Schur operator to be invertible.

load_bearing.statement: For s>0, m(s)=coth(s)−1/s and c_*=min{1/(3 sinh 1),coth 1−1}>0 satisfy c_* min{s,1}≤m(s)<1 and m(s)≤s/2. Consequently 0<(c_*/2)min{h²/(2ε),h/|b|}≤τ<h/(2|b|), and τ≤h²/(8ε).

For the homogeneous one-dimensional model and exact C2 solution, a_h(u,v_h)=F_h(v_h). For every v_h∈V_h, a_h(v_h,v_h)=ε||v_h′||₂²+τb²Σ_K||v_h′||₂,K². This is a squared norm, and the finite-dimensional SUPG system has a unique solution.

On the stated shape-regular affine simplicial mesh family, for u∈C2(closure Ω) and M_2=|Ω|^(1/2)||D²u||∞, the nodal interpolant satisfies ||u−I_hu||₂≤C_I h²M_2 and ||∇(u−I_hu)||₂≤C_I hM_2, with C_I depending only on dimension and shape regularity. Zero boundary data are preserved.
The Galerkin form is augmented by Σ_K δ_K(R_K(w),b·∇v_h)_K, where R_K(w)=−εΔ_Kw+b·∇w+cw, with the matching stabilized load and the stated parameter scaling giving δ_K||c||∞,K²≤ω/4.

With G=A_ff^−1, an exact Schur solution u_c, r_f=F_f−A_fc u_c and invertible approximate Schur operator S̃, the coarse error is at most ||S̃^−1||||A_cf||||T−G||||r_f||. The fine error is at most ||T−G||||r_f||+||T||||A_fc||||ũ_c−u_c||.

On the periodic 2×2 unit-square Q1 mesh, nodal values (−1)^(i+j) define a nonzero mean-zero pressure orthogonal to every Q1 velocity divergence, while its pressure-gradient stabilization equals (8/3)Σ_K τ_K>0.

published_dependencies.used_for: Affine simplex geometry, matching interfaces and the inradius-based shape-regularity convention used by the multidimensional model and interpolation proof.
The explicit Countable Choice assumptions inherited through the published Gauss–Green and derivative-interpolation suppliers.
Cellwise integration by parts in multidimensional SUPG consistency and the convection energy identity; its C1 flux and Countable Choice hypotheses match the uses.
The estimate ||(u−I_hu)′||₂≤h||u″||∞ and endpoint preservation in the one-dimensional energy-error theorem.
Contextual inspection of the published variational-crimes prerequisite. The assigned SUPG proofs derive their estimates directly and do not invoke this theorem.

concerns.concern: The Definition allows “Ω⊂R^d [to] have a finite cell partition” without boundedness, finite cell measure or integrability assumptions on the polynomial spaces, then says “For well-defined cell integrals, take σ∈L∞ ... β∈L∞ ... f∈L2”. These coefficient assumptions alone do not suffice on the literal stated domain. For example, Ω=R^d with one cell, V_h spanned by a nonzero constant vector, Q_h={0}, σ=1, β=0 and f=0 satisfy the listed conditions, but (σu_h,v_h)_Ω is infinite for that constant trial/test pair. Specify bounded finite-element cells or adequate space integrability so B_h is a real bilinear form. The bounded simplicial theorem and finite periodic examples do not exhibit this problem.

The title is “Overlarge streamline stabilization suppresses a one-cell solution”, whereas the Example explicitly uses “one interior P1 degree of freedom on the two-cell mesh h=1/2”. The verification also uses derivatives +2 and −2 on two cells. The computation is sound; the title confuses one degree of freedom with one cell.

seams_checked.note: Read both page bodies and the finite-step MINI existence/energy theorem. This is a contextual page prerequisite: no assigned item imports a Navier–Stokes energy, pressure or convergence result. The supplier uses evolutionary MINI spaces, symmetric-gradient viscosity and skew convection; the consumer independently defines stationary equal-order PSPG with gradient viscosity. Neither page identifies these forms or transfers the supplier's stability conclusions to PSPG.
